finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of ownership. authorized() returns a boolean that is discarded, so an authenticated non-owner, non-admin user can delete another user's project.
finding.source: req.params.id (path parameter), with the caller's session identity in req.user. Precondition: an authenticated user who is neither owner nor admin. The auth middleware is not in the repo, so authentication is assumed.
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, a destructive write on a resource the caller does not own.

trace.note: req.store.projects.get(req.params.id) loads any project with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) called; its boolean result is discarded
authorized() returns resource.ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true and never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at api.js:4-10 throws 403 but is not called on this route. authorized() at api.js:12-14 computes the correct owner-or-admin check, but its result is ignored. No ownership filter on the store lookup. No upstream authorization middleware visible in this repo. The PUT /projects/:id/name handler at api.js:25 correctly uses authorize() and was not flagged.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorized() at api.js:12-14 computes the owner-or-admin check, but its boolean is discarded as a bare statement at api.js:18. authorize() (api.js:4-10, which throws 403) is not called on the DELETE route. No router.use or other authorization middleware exists in the repo (grep found none).
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:16-19 loads the project with no ownership filter (api.js:17), discards the result of authorized() at api.js:18, and deletes at api.js:19, so any authenticated non-owner non-admin user can delete another user's project; the only assumed control is authentication, which does not block a low-privilege user.
